title: Allergic Rhinitis — Initial Presentation
desc: MA workflow for rooming a patient presenting with allergic rhinitis: contraindications, skin testing setup, and SLIT vs SCIT immunotherapy counseling.

blocks.content: When a patient presents with allergic rhinitis symptoms, confirm the following at rooming before the provider enters.
Rooming confirmations
History of food allergies or insect bite allergies
History of asthma
Currently taking beta blockers — this is a contraindication to allergy skin testing and must be flagged
blocks.note: Beta blockade reduces the effectiveness of epinephrine if anaphylaxis occurs

blocks.content: Currently taking any sedating medications (benzodiazepines, sleep aids, certain anxiety medications) — these may need to be held before skin testing
Prepare flexible laryngoscopy setup unless the patient also presents with sinusitis symptoms, in which case follow the sinusitis rooming protocol instead.
Set up for allergy skin testing (intradermal/prick testing per ITF protocol)
HPI documentation
Present the patient's allergy skin testing results in words for the provider to incorporate into the HPI note.
Confirm the patient's current allergy medications — antihistamines, nasal sprays, and irrigation. Document what they are currently using and compliance.
Immunotherapy counseling
Briefly explain both options to the patient before the provider enters so the provider visit is efficient. Document which option the patient prefers in the HPI.
SLIT (Sublingual Immunotherapy)
Not covered by insurance
Cost is approximately $150 per 2-month supply, pay as they go
A few drops placed under the tongue each day, held for 1–2 minutes, then swallowed
No food or drink for 30 minutes after application
Patient must carry an epinephrine auto-injector at all times for the first new dose every 2 months
The patient's very first dose is administered in our allergy department — patient sits for 20 minutes of observation, then takes the vial home
Patient must bring their epinephrine injector to the first allergy appointment
SCIT (Subcutaneous Immunotherapy — Allergy Shots)
Mostly covered by insurance — verify coverage under Chart Notes in the EMR before counseling
Weekly injection schedule
Patient must have a responsible adult present who can drive them to the ER in case of anaphylactic reaction — patients who live alone or cannot guarantee an adult driver are not candidates for shots
Serum must be refrigerated at all times — not advised for frequent travelers
A test wheal (mini skin test) with the allergy serum is required before starting; this is done weekly for the first month with our allergy department
Serum can be delivered to the patient's home but shipping costs apply
Patient must bring their epinephrine injector to the first allergy appointment for the test wheal
Document the patient's preferred therapy option in the HPI.
